subject: Clarify order form indemnity: routing, insurance, and evidence timeline
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@netwise.io>
To: sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@netwise.io, carlos.m@netwise.io
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity language questions on MSA / order form

Sean — thanks for the call earlier. Procurement reviewed the draft MSA + order form and we have two main asks on indemnity before we can move to legal: 1) clarify who controls third-party IP defenses (right to defend vs. reimburse), and 2) confirm evidence/notice SLAs and what we'll need to provide if a claim arises.

Quick notes: 
- We cannot accept open-ended indemnity without either defense control or an explicit insurance offset.
- We will need an evidence checklist to align internal teams (security, legal, ops).

Can your legal rep share an operational timeline and a short list of required items (e.g., DMARC logs, model provenance notes, sample outputs) to speed our SOC-procurement review?

Appreciate it — can we get a short summary by tomorrow EOD so we can plan our internal SOW signatures?

— Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement
Netwise Systems

From: sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Indemnity language questions on MSA / order form

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding Netwise questions. They want clarity on: defense control (we usually take defense for third-party IP claims with cooperation), insurance offsets, and a concrete evidence checklist for procurement. Connor, can ops confirm what we can realistically produce within 10 business days?

My read: we should offer right-to-defend with standard cooperation obligations, preserve the order-form cap, and offer a limited insurance-offset where available (subject to certificate). But procurement will push for customer control + notice-based triggers.

Can legal propose a short paragraph for the order form (2–3 sentences) and a one-page evidence checklist we can send to Netwise? They asked for something by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Indemnity language questions on MSA / order form

Thanks Sean. Draft proposal below — short, operational, and aligned with our playbook. I attach a redline to the MSA (Netwise_MSA_redline.pdf) and an evidence checklist (evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx). High level: 

1) Defense control: Redwood proposes the classic "right to defend" for third-party IP claims with a cooperation clause. We will accept a limited customer review period (10 business days) to propose counsel if there is a material conflict; otherwise Redwood will proceed.

2) Insurance offset: we accept that a court-ordered award or settlement will be reduced by any insurance proceeds recoverable by the claimant; however, insurance will not be used to reduce Redwood's expressed indemnity obligations beyond the award amount. We will provide COI on request.

3) Evidence & notice timeline: customer must provide written notice within 30 days of becoming aware of a claim, and must preserve relevant system logs and samples. Our checklist calls out: notice template, sample outputs (with timestamps), model/config provenance (model id/version), and access contacts for engineering triage.

If Netwise insists on customer control of defense, propose we offer a hybrid: customer may control defense for non-material claims under $25k; Redwood reserves defense for larger claims and those implicating the model. That concession is negotiable but should be limited and tied to an explicit escrow/indemnity cap change.

I'll keep the redline tight — aim to send both attachments to Netwise under my signature. Sean: flag if you want a softer customer-facing framing.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
(attachment: Netwise_MSA_redline.pdf, evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@netwise.io>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@netwise.io, carlos.m@netwise.io
Date: Wed, 6 Mar 2029 07:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity language questions on MSA / order form

Kimberly — appreciate the quick redline and checklist. A few follow-ups after internal counsel review: 

- The 30-day notice is acceptable but we need a minor clarification: notice should be "promptly, and in any event within 30 days of receipt" so it covers staggered discovery.
- The hybrid defense proposal is a reasonable starting point, but legal wants a clearer $ threshold and a requirement that customer counsel be "substantially similar" in experience if they propose alternate counsel.
- Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a sample COI (pdf) showing the types of coverage and limits you rely on for the insurance-offset language.

Netwise can accept receipt of an evidence checklist + COI and will circulate to legal. Can you also provide an operational timeline for evidence delivery (we expect items within 10 business days after notice in most cases)?

If we can get the redline + COI this morning, procurement will circulate to leadership and we can target signature next week.

— Elena

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@netwise.io>, sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 6 Mar 2029 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity language questions on MSA / order form

Elena — thanks. Attaching the requested COI (certificate_of_insurance.pdf) and an updated redline that adopts your "promptly, and in any event within 30 days" wording. Operational commitments: 

- Evidence delivery timeline: Redwood will make good-faith operational efforts to deliver the checklist items within 10 business days of receipt of a valid notice; certain items that require deeper diagnostics (e.g., internal audit logs older than 90 days) may require up to 20 business days.
- Counsel experience: we accept the "substantially similar" requirement for alternate customer counsel proposals; if a conflict exists we will use the 10-business-day review window.
- Threshold: we will accept customer control for claims below $25,000 only if customer agrees to an explicit carve-in clause in the order form that increases the order-form cap to $500k for that scenario.

Actions: 
- Attached: Netwise_MSA_redline.pdf (updated), evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx (unchanged), certificate_of_insurance.pdf
- Sean: please confirm if we should offer the $25k / $500k hybrid tradeoff in the customer-facing email. I suggest yes — it gives procurement a clear economic lever and preserves our protection for larger claims.

Best,
— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
(attachments: Netwise_MSA_redline.pdf, evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx, certificate_of_insurance.pdf)
